methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+. The target operates within a sector comprising one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and anchors the valuation. Using total capital raised of $575M as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage companies progressing to their next funding round yields an implied valuation of $690M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable; while eight same-sector peers exist, none satisfy narrow filters for stage alignment, adjacency, or valuation-tier similarity. Restricting to an insufficiently populated peer set would introduce bias; an all-sector median approach would lack granularity.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $586M (low) to $793M (high), with a central estimate of $690M. This range reflects the single applicable method and the methodological constraint that peer comparables lack sufficient density within VulcanForms' specific stage and sub-vertical. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage robotics comparables and reliance on historical stage-transition multiples that may not capture current market conditions in frontier manufacturing technology.
